title: God sent the eternal Son as Mediator-surety
source_text: VIII. Hinc est quod Deus Optimus Maximus generis humani misertus, illudque ex debita perditione eripere volens, aeternum suum Filium, & eundem cum ipso Deum in mundum misit, qui in personam eandem assumpta natura humana, ac proinde simul verus Deus & verus homo, per omnia nobis similis existens, sese pro nobis Deo Patri Mediatorem & sponsorem obtulit, qui poenas nobis debitas exantlaret, iramque divinam a nobis averteret, justitiae divinae pro nobis satisfaciendo.
pass_a_gloss: Hence it is that God Most Good and Great, pitying the human race and willing to snatch it from due perdition, sent his eternal Son—the same God with himself—into the world, who, having assumed human nature into the same person, and thus at once true God and true man, existing like us in all things, offered himself for us to God the Father as Mediator and surety, to exhaust the penalties due to us, turn away divine wrath from us, and satisfy divine justice for us.
pass_b_english: God sent his eternal Son—true God and true man—as Mediator and surety.
He exhausts our due penalties, turns wrath, and satisfies divine justice for us.
